postosuchus:research:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (research: General pseudosuchian research)

facts.statement: The genus Postosuchus was described by Chatterjee in 1985.
facts.quote: authority: Chatterjee, 1985

facts.statement: Postosuchus lived in North America during the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Postosuchus (meaning "crocodile from Post") is an extinct genus of rauisuchid that lived in what is now North America during the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Postosuchus belongs to the clade Pseudosuchia and includes two species: P. kirkpatricki and P. alisonae.
facts.quote: The genus comprises two species, P. kirkpatricki and P. alisonae, and belongs to the clade Pseudosuchia, the archosaur lineage that includes modern crocodilians.

facts.statement: The name Postosuchus refers to Post Quarry in Texas, where fossils of the type species were found.
facts.quote: The name refers to Post Quarry in Texas, where numerous fossils of the type species, P. kirkpatricki, were discovered.

facts.statement: Postosuchus was an apex predator in the Triassic that was larger than small contemporary dinosaurs like Coelophysis.
facts.quote: Postosuchus was one of the apex predators of its region during the Triassic, exceeding contemporary small predatory dinosaurs such as Coelophysis in size.

facts.statement: Postosuchus likely preyed on large herbivores such as dicynodonts and small early dinosaurs.
facts.quote: It likely preyed on large herbivores including dicynodonts, as well as small early dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Postosuchus had a robust skeleton with a deep skull and long tail, reaching an estimated length of 5 to 6 meters or more.
facts.quote: It had a robust skeleton, a deep skull and a long tail and reached an estimated length of 5 - 6 m or more.

facts.statement: The pelvis of Postosuchus featured a hooked pubis and rod-like ischium similar to those of carnosaurs.
facts.quote: The pelvis with the hooked pubis and the rod-like ischium looked like those of carnosaurs.

facts.statement: Some Postosuchus fossils show ribs associated with gastralia, which are dermal bones in the ventral body region.
facts.quote: In some discoveries, ribs were found associated with gastralia, dermal bones located in the ventral region of the body.

facts.statement: Postosuchus had a massively built skull with dagger-like teeth that was narrow in front and wide and deep behind.
facts.quote: Postosuchus had a massively built skull, bearing dagger-like teeth, which was constructed narrow in front, and extended wide and deep behind.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Postosuchus measured 55 cm in length and 21 cm in breadth and depth.
facts.quote: The holotype skull was 55 cm in length and 21 cm broad and deep.

facts.statement: Postosuchus jaws held large, sharp, serrated teeth, some of which were developed into hooked sabers.
facts.quote: The jaws held large and sharp, serrated teeth, of which some were developed even larger to operate as hooked sabers.

facts.statement: Postosuchus possessed heterodont dentition, meaning each tooth differed in size and shape from the others.
facts.quote: Postosuchus possessed heterodonty dentition, which means each tooth was different in size and shape from the others.

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Postosuchus contained 17 teeth on each side, with four on each premaxilla and 13 on each maxilla.
facts.quote: The upper jaw contained 17 teeth on each side, with each premaxilla bearing only four teeth and each maxilla 13 teeth.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Postosuchus had over 30 teeth.
facts.quote: The lower jaw had over 30 teeth.

facts.statement: Postosuchus tooth replacement differed from crocodiles, as new teeth grew until the old ones were fully resorbed rather than fitting directly into their pulp cavities.
facts.quote: Replacement activity in Postosuchus was different from that of crocodiles, since the replacement tooth did not fit directly in the pulp cavity of the old tooth, but grew until resorption of the old tooth was complete.

facts.statement: Postosuchus had forelimbs about 64% the size of its hind limbs, with small hands that had five toes and a single claw on the first digit.
facts.quote: With the forelimbs being about 64% the size of the hind limbs, Postosuchus had small hands bearing five toes, of which only the first digit bore a claw.

facts.statement: Postosuchus had feet much larger than its hands, featuring a fifth metatarsal bone shaped like a hook.
facts.quote: The feet were much larger than the hands, with the fifth metatarsal forming a hook shape.

facts.statement: As a crurotarsan, Postosuchus possessed a heel and ankle structure similar to that of modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: As it was a crurotarsan, the heel and ankle of Postosuchus resemble those of modern crocodiles.

facts.statement: Postosuchus had limbs positioned underneath its body, resulting in an upright stance.
facts.quote: The limbs were located underneath the body, giving Postosuchus an upright stance.

facts.statement: Historically, scientists debated whether rauisuchids like Postosuchus were primarily bipedal or quadrupedal.
facts.quote: Historically, there has been debate over whether or not rauisuchids like Postosuchus were mainly bipedal or quadrupedal.

facts.statement: A 2013 study suggested Postosuchus was an obligate biped based on its digit, vertebrae, and pelvis anatomy.
facts.quote: In 2013, a major study of the skeletal structure concluded that Postosuchus may have been an obligate biped based on the anatomy of the digits, vertebrae, and pelvis.

facts.statement: A 2015 study found load-bearing adaptations in the hands of Postosuchus, supporting the idea that its forelimbs were used for weight support.
facts.quote: However, a 2015 study noted several load-bearing adaptations present in the manus of Postosuchus, substantiating the view that its manus was used for support.

facts.statement: In 1980, Texas Tech University paleontologists discovered a fossil-rich site near Post, Texas, yielding a dozen specimens of a new rauisuchid.
facts.quote: During an expedition in 1980, paleontologists of the Texas Tech University discovered a new geological site rich in fossils near Post, Garza County, Texas, US, where a dozen well-preserved specimens belonging to a new rauisuchid were found.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Sankar Chatterjee described the holotype of Postosuchus kirkpatricki (specimen TTUP 9000) in 1985.
facts.quote: The holotype of P. kirkpatricki (TTUP 9000), representing a well-preserved skull and a partial postcranial skeleton, was described along with other findings of this new genus by paleontologist Sankar Chatterjee in 1985.

facts.statement: Peyer and colleagues described the new species Postosuchus alisonae in 2008.
facts.quote: In 2008, Peyer and colleagues described a new species of Postosuchus, P. alisonae.

facts.statement: Postosuchus alisonae was discovered in 1992 by students Brian Coffey and Marco Brewer at a quarry in Durham County, North Carolina.
facts.quote: This new species was discovered in 1992 by two UNC undergrad students, Brian Coffey and Marco Brewer, at Triangle Brick Co. Quarry, in Durham County, North Carolina.

facts.statement: The function of the single claw on Postosuchus's first digit is uncertain, though it may have aided in grappling prey.
facts.quote: Due to the diminutive size of the hands, whether this claw was especially predominant in predation is uncertain, but it may have helped in grappling prey.

facts.statement: Well-preserved remains of Postosuchus alisonae provided new insights into previously unknown anatomical parts of the genus.
facts.quote: The well-preserved remains of P. alisonae shed new light on parts of Postosuchus anatomy, which were previously not well known.

facts.statement: Differences in hand bones between P. kirkpatricki and P. alisonae support the theory that some fossils previously assigned to Postosuchus actually belong to different animals.
facts.quote: Moreover, the well-preserved remains of P. alisonae shed new light on parts of Postosuchus anatomy, which were previously not well known. Specifically, the differences between the manus bones of P. kirkpatricki and P. alisonae confirm the chimera theory (associated fossils belonging to different animals) suggested by Long and Murry.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows a Postosuchus positioned on top of a Dromicosuchus skeleton with tooth marks on the skull and neck, indicating predation.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the Postosuchus was positioned on top of a skeleton of the sphenosuchian Dromicosuchus, which included tooth marks on the skull and neck.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. alisonae preserved gut contents including bones from at least four other animals, such as an aetosaur and a cynodont.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of P. alisonae (UNC 15575) is also unusual in its preservation of gut contents: bones from at least four other animals, including a partial skeleton of an aetosaur, a snout, coracoid, and humerus of the traversodontid cynodont Plinthogomphodon, two phalanges from a dicynodont, and a possible temnospondyl bone.

facts.statement: Many juvenile skeletons originally assigned to Postosuchus kirkpatricki were reclassified by Long and Murry as a distinct genus named Chatterjeea elegans.
facts.quote: Subsequently, some specimens (such manus and toe bones) were re-assigned to Chatterjeea and Lythrosuchus; Long and Murry pointed out that many of the juvenile skeletons (TTUP 9003-9011), which Chatterjee assigned to P. kirkpatricki, belong to a distinct genus, which they named Chatterjeea elegans.

facts.statement: In 2006, Nesbitt and Norell argued that the genus Chatterjeea is a junior synonym of Shuvosaurus.
facts.quote: Furthermore, in 2006 Nesbitt and Norell argued that Chatterjeea is a junior synonym of Shuvosaurus.

facts.statement: Postosuchus kirkpatricki is a rauisuchid from the late Triassic period.
facts.quote: The holotype of P. kirkpatricki (TTUP 9000), representing a well-preserved skull and a partial postcranial skeleton, was described along with other findings of this new genus by paleontologist Sankar Chatterjee in 1985.

facts.statement: Specimens similar to Postosuchus were discovered in Crosby County, Texas, in 1920 and described by Ermine Cowles Case in 1922.
facts.quote: Putative occurrences Specimens similar to Postosuchus were discovered in Crosby County, Texas, in 1920, and described by paleontologist Ermine Cowles Case in 1922.

facts.statement: Early findings from 1932 to 1943 were initially classified as a new phytosaur reptile before being assigned to Postosuchus 40 years later.
facts.quote: These early findings, from 1932 to 1943, were initially referred to as a new phytosaur reptile, but assigned 40 years later to Postosuchus.

facts.statement: Postosuchus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the Norian to Rhaetian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Triásico Superior (Noriense - Rhaetiense)

facts.statement: Postosuchus lived in what is now North America approximately 221 to 203 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivieron en lo que ahora es Norteamérica durante el Triásico Superior (hace unos 221-203millones de años)

facts.statement: The genus Postosuchus was established by Chatterjee in 1985.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Chatterjee, 1985

facts.statement: Postosuchus is a member of the clade Pseudosuchia, the lineage of archosaurs that includes modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Postosuchus es un miembro del clado Pseudosuchia, el linaje de arcosaurios que incluye a los actuales crocodilianos

facts.statement: The name Postosuchus means "Post crocodile", named after the Post locality in Texas.
facts.quote: Postosuchus (nombre que significa "cocodrilo de Post", por la localidad de Post, Texas)

facts.statement: The skeleton of Postosuchus was large and robust, featuring a high skull and a long tail.
facts.quote: El esqueleto de Postosuchus es grande y robusto con un cráneo alto y una cola larga.

facts.statement: Postosuchus was one of the largest carnivorous reptiles of the Late Triassic, reaching over 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Postosuchus fue uno de los mayores reptiles carnívoros durante el Triásico Superior, alcanzando más de 4m de longitud.

facts.statement: In life, the animal may have weighed between 250 and 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: En vida el animal pudo haber pesado entre 250 a 300kg.

facts.statement: It had an enormous skull equipped with dagger-like teeth.
facts.quote: Tenía un enorme cráneo que portaba dientes similares a dagas.

facts.statement: It was a hunter that fed on large prey such as dicynodonts and many other creatures smaller than itself.
facts.quote: Era un cazador que se alimentaba de grandes presas como los dicinodontes y muchas otras criaturas menores que él mismo.

facts.statement: It was one of the super-predators of the area during the Triassic, larger than the small predatory dinosaurs of its time, such as Coelophysis.
facts.quote: Fue uno de los superdepredadores de esta área durante el Triásico, mayor que los pequeños dinosaurios depredadores de su época (tales como Coelophysis).

facts.statement: The front limbs of Postosuchus measured just over half the size of its hind limbs.
facts.quote: Los miembros delanteros de Postosuchus medían poco más de la mitad del tamaño de sus extremidades posteriores.

facts.statement: There is a debate over whether Postosuchus was indeed bipedal or quadrupedal, with no consensus among scientists.
facts.quote: Existe un debate sobre si Postosuchus era en efecto bípedo o cuadrúpedo, sin que haya un consenso entre los científicos al respecto.

facts.statement: In 2002, David J. Gower argued that a braincase assigned to Postosuchus was incomplete and might actually belong to an ornithodire.
facts.quote: In the case of the braincase later assigned to Postosuchus, in 2002, paleontologist David J. Gower argued that the specimen is not complete and may belong to an ornithodire.

facts.statement: Postosuchus lived in a tropical, moist, and warm environment containing ferns, gymnosperms, and cycads.
facts.quote: Postosuchus lived in a tropical environment. The moist and warm region consisted of ferns, such as Cynepteris, Phelopteris, and Clathropteris, gymnosperms represented by Pelourdea, Araucarioxylon, Woodworthia, Otozamites, and Dinophyton, and cycads such as Sanmiguelia.

facts.statement: Postosuchus was one of the largest animals in its ecosystem and preyed on upland herbivores like the dicynodont Placerias.
facts.quote: Postosuchus was one of the largest animals in that ecosystem and preyed on herbivores in the uplands, such as the dicynodont Placerias.

facts.statement: The skull of Postosuchus was narrow at the front and extended upward and backward.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Postosuchus era de forma estrecha en el frente y se extendía hacia arriba y a lo ancho en su parte posterior.

facts.statement: The skull measured 55 cm in length and 21 cm in width and height.
facts.quote: Medía 55 cm de longitud y 21 cm de anchura y altura.

facts.statement: Postosuchus likely had good distance vision due to large eye orbits and a keen sense of smell from its elongated nostrils.
facts.quote: Postosuchus debió de tener una vista a distancia, gracias a las grandes órbitas en las que se situarían grandes ojos, y un buen olfato proporcionado por sus alargadas narinas.

facts.statement: A hole under the nostrils likely housed the Jacobson's organ, a special olfactory organ sometimes called the "sixth sense".
facts.quote: Dentro del cráneo, bajo las narinas, había un agujero que probablemente alojaba el órgano de Jacobson, un órgano olfatorio especial a veces conocido como el "sexto sentido".

facts.statement: Its jaws had large serrated teeth that were sometimes developed enough to function like sabers.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas tenían grandes dientes aserrados y en algunos puntos era lo bastante desarrollados como para servir a modo de sables.

facts.statement: A complete tooth found in North Carolina measured nearly 7.2 cm in height.
facts.quote: Un diente completo encontrado entre restos de Postosuchus en Carolina del Norte medía cerca de 7.2 cm de altura.

facts.statement: Postosuchus had heterodont dentition, meaning each tooth was distinct in size and shape compared to others.
facts.quote: Postosuchus tenía una dentición heterodonta, lo que significa que cada diente era distinto en tamaño y forma con respecto a los otros.

facts.statement: The upper jaw contained seventeen teeth, divided into just four premaxillary and thirteen maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: En la mandíbula superior había diecisiete dientes, dividiéndose en apenas cuatro premaxilares y trece dientes maxilares.

facts.statement: The lower jaw contained nearly thirty teeth.
facts.quote: En la mandíbula inferior se contaban cerca de treinta dientes.

facts.statement: The neck consisted of at least eight cervical vertebrae followed by sixteen dorsal ones, while four fused sacral vertebrae supported the hips.
facts.quote: El cuello de Postosuchus consiste de al menos ocho vértebras cervicales seguidas por dieciséis dorsales, mientras que cuatro vértebras sacrales co-osificadas apoyaban las caderas.

facts.statement: It is believed they had more than thirty caudal vertebrae in the tail that reduced in size toward the posterior end.
facts.quote: Se cree que tenían más de treinta vértebras caudales en la cola que se reducían de tamaño hacia el extremo posterior.

facts.statement: The pelvis, with a hook-shaped pubis and bar-shaped ischium, resembled that of carnivorous dinosaurs.
facts.quote: La pelvis con el hueso púbico en forma de gancho y el isquion en forma de barra se parecía a la de los dinosaurios carnosaurios.

facts.statement: Paleontologists found osteoderms, which were thick plates forming scales, alongside the skeleton remains.
facts.quote: Junto a los restos del esqueleto, los paleontólogos también encontraron osteodermos, los cuales eran gruesas placas que formaban escamas.

facts.statement: These osteoderms were found along the neck, back, and possibly over or under the tail.
facts.quote: Se encontraban a lo largo de su cuello, espalda y posiblemente sobre o bajo la cola.

facts.statement: Its limbs were positioned under the body, giving Postosuchus an upright posture.
facts.quote: Las extremidades se localizaban bajo el cuerpo dándole a Postosuchus una postura erguida.

facts.statement: With forelimbs measuring approximately 64% of the hindlimbs, Postosuchus had small hands with five fingers.
facts.quote: Con las extremidades anteriores midiendo aproximadamente el 64% de las posteriores, Postosuchus tenía manos pequeñas que tenían cinco dedos.

facts.statement: Only the first finger had a large claw used as an offensive weapon, though the robust forelimbs were likely used to hold prey.
facts.quote: Solo el primer dedo tenía una garra grande, que se usaba como arma ofensiva, aunque los miembros delanteros eran robustos, probablemente para sostener a la presa.

facts.statement: The feet were much larger than the hands, with the fifth metatarsian forming a hook shape.
facts.quote: Los pies eran mucho más grandes que las manos, con el quinto metatarsiano formando una forma de gancho.

facts.statement: As a crurotarsan, the ankle and heel of Postosuchus resembled those of modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: Como un crurotarso, el tobillo y el talón de Postosuchus se parecían al de los cocodrilos modernos.

facts.statement: Remains of Postosuchus were first discovered in Crosby County and described by paleontologist Ermine Cowles Case in 1922.
facts.quote: Los restos de Postosuchus se descubrieron por primera vez en el condado de Crosby, y fueron descritos por el paleontólogo Ermine Cowles Case en 1922.

facts.statement: Originally, fossils found of Postosuchus were considered to belong to a dinosaur.
facts.quote: Originalmente se consideró que los fósiles hallados de Postosuchus pertenecían a un dinosaurio.

facts.statement: Case mistakenly assigned them to the dinosaur genus Coelophysis.
facts.quote: Case los confundió asignándolos al género de dinosaurio Coelophysis.

facts.statement: Postosuchus has been found only in the United States, in the states of Arizona, New Mexico, North Carolina, and Texas.
facts.quote: Postosuchus ha sido descubierto solo en Estados Unidos, en los estados de Arizona, Nuevo México, Carolina del Norte y Texas.

facts.statement: The holotype of P. kirkpatricki (TTUP 9000), represented by a well-preserved skull and partial postcranial skeleton, was described by paleontologist Sankar Chatterjee in 1985.
facts.quote: El holotipo de P. kirkpatricki (TTUP 9000), representado por un cráneo bien preservado y un esqueleto postcraneal parcial, fue descrito junto con otros hallazgos de este nuevo género por el paleontólogo Sankar Chatterjee en 1985.

facts.statement: Chatterjee named the species after Jack Kirkpatrick, who assisted during fieldwork.
facts.quote: Chatterjee dio el nombre a la especie por Jack Kirkpatrick, quien ayudó durante su trabajo de campo.

facts.statement: In 2008, Peyer et al. described a new species of Postosuchus, P. alisonae, discovered in 1992 at Triangle Brick Co. Quarry in Durham County, North Carolina.
facts.quote: En 2008, Peyer et al., describieron una nueva especie de Postosuchus, P. alisonae, que fue descubierta en 1992 en Triangle Brick Co. Quarry, Condado de Durham, Carolina del Norte.

facts.statement: The species name refers to Alison L. Chambers, who worked to popularize paleontology in North Carolina.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se refiere a Alison L. Chambers, quien trabajó para popularizar la paleontología en Carolina del Norte.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of P. alisonae (UNC 15575) is unusual for preserving intestinal contents: bones of at least four other animals, including a partial aetosaur skeleton, a snout, coracoid and humerus of the traversodont cynodont Plinthogomphodon, two phalanges of a dicynodont, and a possible temnospondyl bone.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de P. alisonae (UNC 15575) es también inusual por la preservación de contenidos intestinales: huesos de al menos otros cuatro animales, incluyendo un esqueleto parcial de un aetosaurio, un hocico, coracoides y húmero del cinodonte traversodóntido Plinthogomphodon, dos falanges de un dicinodonte, y un posible hueso de temnospóndilo.

facts.statement: P. alisonae represents the largest rauisuchian reptile recovered from that quarry and the first articulated rauisuchian archosaur found in eastern North America.
facts.quote: P. alisonae representa el mayor reptil suquio recuperado de esa cantera y el primer espécimen articulado de un arcosaurio rauisuquio hallado en el este de Norteamérica.

facts.statement: In 2002, David J. Gower claimed the later-assigned neurocranium was incomplete and might not belong to an ornithodiran.
facts.quote: En el caso del neurocráneo más tarde asignado a Postosuchus, en 2002 David J. Gower afirmó que el espécimen no estaba completo y que podía no pertenecer a un ornitódiro.

facts.statement: In other research, paleontologists suggested that some bones (such as hand and foot digits) described by Chatterjee in 1985 are a combination of remains belonging to Chatterjeea, Lythrosuchus, and Postosuchus.
facts.quote: En otras investigaciones, los paleontólogos sugirieron que algunos huesos (como los de los dedos de la mano y el pie) descritos por Chatterjee en 1985, son una combinación de restos pertenecientes a Chatterjeea, Lythrosuchus y Postosuchus.

facts.statement: Long and Murry also noted that many juvenile skeletons (TTUP 9003-9011) assigned by Chatterjee to P. kirkpatricki belonged to a different genus and species named Chatterjeea elegans.
facts.quote: Long y Murry también señalaron que muchos de los esqueletos juveniles (TTUP 9003-9011), que Chatterjee asignó a P. kirkpatricki, pertenecían a un género y especie distintos, nombrado Chatterjeea elegans.

facts.statement: Furthermore, in 2006 Nesbitt and Norell asserted that Chatterjeea is a more modern synonym of Shuvosaurus.
facts.quote: Más aún, en 2006 Nesbitt y Norell afirmaron que Chatterjeea es un sinónimo más moderno de Shuvosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1943, Case described a pelvis with a pubis (UM 23127) from the Dockum Group in Texas, dating from the Carnian to early Norian at the end of the Triassic period.
facts.quote: En 1943, Case de nuevo describió una pelvis junto con un pubis (UM 23127) en el Grupo Dockum de Texas, que data desde el Carniense hasta principios del Noriense a fines del período Triásico.

facts.statement: The first articulated skeleton referred to P. kirkpatricki (CM 73372) was recovered by David S. Berman of the Carnegie Museum of Natural History from the Coelophysis quarry in Ghost Ranch, New Mexico, between 1988 and 1989.
facts.quote: El primer esqueleto articulado referido a P. kirkpatricki (CM 73372) fue recuperado por David S. Berman del Museo Carnegie de Historia Natural, en la cantera Coelophysis en Ghost Ranch, Nuevo México, entre 1988 y 1989.

facts.statement: Postosuchus lived in a tropical environment.
facts.quote: Postosuchus vivió en un ambiente tropical.

facts.statement: Large Araucarioxylon specimens indicate the region was abundantly irrigated.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de grandes especímenes pertenecientes a Araucarioxylon determinan que la región estaba abundantemente irrigada.

facts.statement: Postosuchus was one of the largest animals in its ecosystem and preyed on herbivores like Trilophosaurus and Typothorax.
facts.quote: Postosuchus fue uno de los mayores animales en este ecosistema y depredaba a herbívoros como Trilophosaurus y Typothorax.

facts.statement: The genus Postosuchus was named by Chatterjee in 1985.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Postosuchus (genus), Chatterjee 1985

facts.statement: Postosuchus belongs to the parent group Rauisuchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Rauisuchidae

facts.statement: Postosuchus is classified in the family Rauisuchidae.
facts.quote: Family: Rauisuchidae

facts.statement: Postosuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.quote: Type species: Postosuchus kirkpatricki

facts.statement: Postosuchus lived from the Carnian to the Rhaetian stages, between 237 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Rhaetian (237 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Postosuchus lived in highlands alongside Coelophysis and other archosaurs such as Desmatosuchus and Typothorax.
facts.quote: Postosuchus vivió en las tierras altas junto con Coelophysis y otros arcosaurios como Desmatosuchus y Typothorax.
